#2742. NFL news, live updates: Ravens name undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano starting QB; Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love headed to IR with ankle injury; Lions LB Jack Campbell remains hospitalized with neck injury

Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season is nearly a wrap, with just the Chicago Bears and Seattle Seahawks left to play on "Monday Night Football."

There was plenty of excitement on Sunday, including two games that went into overtime, but they unfortunately weren't without injuries. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson made his return to the lineup after rehabbing an ankle injury, but that excitement was short-lived, as he suffered a thumb injury on his first pass attempt of the game. Per head coach Jesse Minter, he'll require surgery and a stint on the injured reserve list — a brutal blow.

Backup Tyler Huntley is also dealing with a turf toe injury, which forced Baltimore to resort to their emergency third quarterback, Joe Fagnano. He completed 10-of-21 passes for 91 yards and an interception in relief of Jackson and Huntley.

The Ravens are playing on a short week, as they're set to host the Jacksonville Jaguars on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 9, and Fagnano will officially be QB1 for that matchup. The 25-year-old, who played his college ball at Maine and then UConn, will be the second undrafted rookie to start under center for Baltimore in the Ravens' 32-year history, per ESPN's Jamison Hensley.

The Detroit Lions handed the Minnesota Vikings their first loss of the season, but lost a key playmaker on defense as All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a scary-looking neck injury. He was immobilized on a backboard before being transported to the hospital as his teammates gathered around him in an emotional scene.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 8.

The Colts aren't purging their entire roster.

Per NFL Network, the Colts and defensive lineman Adetomiwa Adebawore have agreed to a $35 million contract extension with a $13 million roster bonus.

The deal adds $22.5 million in new money to his contract through the 2027 season, per the report. Adebawore was previously on track to became a free agent in the offseason at the conclusion of his four-year, $4.6 million rookie contract.

Adebawore, 25, has tied his career high with four sacks through eight games in addition to 19 tackles and eight quarterback hits.

The New Orleans Saints are on the kicker market.

The Saints announced on Tuesday that they have released veteran kicker Daniel Carlson after Carlson missed another field goal in a 16-10 Week 7 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Carlson missed a 52-yard attempt with 9:42 remaining that would have cut Pittsburgh's lead to 16-13. He finished the game hitting 1 of 2 field-goal attempts, dropping his season success rate on field goals to a career-low 66.7% (8 of 12).

For more on the Saints' kicker search, read here.

The Ravens injury woes continue, as the team placed kicker Tyler Loop on the injured reserve list with a groin injury on Tuesday.

Loop has made 13 of 17 field goals attempted this season, having gone 5 for 5 on kicks from 50-plus yards. He missed one field goal in Week 8's loss to the Buffalo Bills from 34 yards.

The team signed kicker Jake Moody to the practice squad on Oct. 20, and he'll presumably step up in Loop's absence.

If officially elevated to the active roster, the Ravens will be Moody's fourth team over the past two seasons. He hopped between the San Francisco 49ers (who selected him in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft), Chicago Bears and Washington Commanders last season, good on 19 of 23 attempts in 2025.

The Buffalo Bills have released safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported on Tuesday. The team then confirmed the move on social media.

Gardner-Johnson served a one-game suspension this past week after spitting on Las Vegas Raiders tight end in Week 6, an action that led to his ejection. The Bills then had a bye in Week 7, which led to him serving that suspension in Week 8.

Gardner-Johnson has been a bit of a journeyman in recent seasons, with the Bills being his sixth team in eight seasons. He started his career with the New Orleans Saints, who drafted him in the fourth round out of Florida. He's also had stints with the Philadelphia Eagles, Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions and Houston Texans.

He started in all six games of his games played for the Bills this past season. Damar Halmin got the start in Gardner Johnson's place while he served his suspension.

Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told the media on Tuesday that the team would start undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

The announcement comes as starting quarterback Lamar Jackson is headed to injured reserve with a thumb injury and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley was diagnosed with turf toe.

Fagnano will be the second undrafted rookie to start under center for Baltimore in the Ravens' 32-year history, per ESPN's Jamison Hensley.

The rookie finished his collegiate career at UConn. He played in 24 games with the Huskies and ended his time with them having accumulated 5,252 passing yards and 48 touchdowns. Fagnano is less mobile than Jackson or Huntley and rushed for just 223 yards and 4 touchdowns on 93 carries at UConn.

Although Baltimore Ravens quarterback Joe Fagnano was spotted wearing a guard/brace on his right ankle Tuesday, as captured by The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec, he was practicing, two days out from a "Thursday Night Football" game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) have already been ruled out for the matchup. Jackson, of course, could be done for the season.

Huntley is navigating what's reportedly thought to be turf toe.

So Fagnano, a 25-year-old undrafted rookie who played his college ball at UConn and Maine, could make his first career NFL start this week, in primetime no less.

Fagnano was listed as a limited participant in the Ravens' walkthrough on Monday. Baltimore signed fellow QB Austin Reed to the practice squad that day.

Arizona Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love is headed to injured reserve with a right high-ankle sprain, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports.

The injury and IR designation will sideline Love for a minimum of four games. The Cardinals have upcoming games against the Seahawks, Rams, Chiefs and Commanders.

Love injured his ankle in Sunday's win over the Dallas Cowboys when his ankle got rolled underneath his body on a tackle. He was able to get up to walk to the sideline, but he did not return to the game as the Cardinals rallied from a 14-3 halftime deficit for a 33-30 overtime win.

Trade rumors have surrounded Arizona Cardinals defensive end Josh Sweat for a while now. NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported Tuesday that the belief around the league is that the 29-year-old Sweat would be open to a trade.

That said, per Schultz, Arizona's asking price is believed to be high, and the team has given the impression that it'd be OK holding onto the pass rusher.

Sweat is in his second season with the Cardinals, who signed him to a four-year contract in free agency last year, a deal reportedly worth $76.4 million, including $41 million guaranteed.

When Sweat arrived in Arizona, he was reuniting with then-Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon, who was previously Sweat's defensive coordinator with the Philadelphia Eagles. But the Cardinals moved on from Gannon after last season. That coaching change raised questions about Sweat's future in the desert.

During the 2025 season, Sweat piled up 12 sacks. He got off to a slow start this time around but has logged 19 total tackles and three sacks in his past five games.

If the Broncos decide they are on a heater in which the coin is repeatedly flipping on their side for a statistically improbable reason, they have some work to do before the trade deadline on Nov. 10. The offense, which has been inconsistent all season and was catching boos from the home crowd Sunday after three straight three-and-outs to start the second half, should be the focus.

Denver is just 30th in yards gained this season. A play-calling change from offensive coordinator Davis Webb to Payton hasn't helped much. The Broncos aren't getting a quarterback to replace Bo Nix but practically every other position group could be a candidate for an upgrade. The defense is good enough for a long playoff run, as it was last season. The variable is the offense.

Or maybe it just doesn't matter. The Broncos have beaten the odds for two seasons. They're 20-5 since the start of the 2025 season and 16 of those wins have been by eight points or less. They continue to laugh at the regression proclamations.

QB3 Joe Fagnano, who finished Sunday's loss to the Bills, was limited during Monday's walkthrough with an ankle injury.

Baltimore has a short week as they take on the Jaguars Thursday night.

The Los Angeles Rams pushed a lot of chips to the middle of the table over the offseason. Then, when they came out of the gates slow, other teams saw an opportunity.

Last week, the Seattle Seahawks made a big move for guard Quenton Nelson and the San Francisco 49ers got a big acquisition in defensive lineman DeForest Buckner. The NFC West got a lot harder.

The Chicago Bears, clearly believing the NFC is up for grabs, traded a couple first-round picks to the Tennessee Titans for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. His stellar play on Monday night in his Bears debut has lifted Chicago's ceiling for this season. Other top NFC teams will inevitably add to their rosters.

The Rams need to look to see if they have any more chips remaining to up their bet.

A pair of Cowboys defensive backs are now in concussion protocol, and linebacker Malachi Lawrence is dealing with an ankle injury.

It's unlcear how long any of them will be sidelined just yet.

Cardinals wide receiver Kendrick Bourne sustained a fractured tibia during Sunday's win over the Cowboys, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports.

The injury will end Bourne's season. It won't require surgery, per the report.

In eight games this season, Bourne has 26 catches for 263 yards with no touchdowns.

Cardinals rookie Jeremiyah love seemingly can't catch a break on the injury front, with head coach Mike LaFleur telling reporters on Monday that the rookie has suffered another ankle injury.

Love missed multiple preseason games with a high right ankle sprain, and missed two games last month with a left ankle injury. However, LaFleur said that the injury Love sustained on Sunday was a new injury, not a re-aggravation of one of his previous knocks.

"This is new, so this is not the left ankle or the right ankle, it's a new portion of the ankle," LaFleur said.

Love exited Sunday's win over the Cowboys after his ankle got rolled under his body on a tackle in the first half. The rookie running back was able to walk to the sideline but slammed his helmet down, clearly frustrated, before heading into the locker room; he did not return to the game.

LaFleur said that he'll give reporters more information on Wednesday, adding that he wanted to get a chance to talk to Love first.

Myles Garrett will return to practice for the Los Angeles Rams this week. Head coach Sean McVay announced the news to reporters Monday.

Garrett's played just one game for the Rams since the blockbuster offseason trade that sent him to Los Angeles from the Cleveland Browns. He underwent knee surgery after struggling to make an impact in the Rams' season-opening loss to the 49ers in Australia and has been sidelined since.

Garrett's planned return to practice doesn't mean he'll be ready to play Sunday against the Washington Commanders. But it's a positive sign for his return to the playing field.

His return to practice from injured reserve opens a 21-day window for Garrett to be elevated to the active roster or placed on season-ending injured reserve.

Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni spoke to the media on Monday. He said he isn't making a change at offensive coordinator, and Sean Mannion will remain in the role.

Philly has lost six straight games. The Eagles took a 10-0 lead over the Commanders on Monday night, but Washington scored 27 consecutive points to win.

Injuries are piling up for Philadelphia. The Eagles are expected to be without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts for the remainder of the season, leaving Tanner McKee currently under center. Saquon Barkley has been nursing a hamstring injury, and Philly was without DeVonta Smith on Monday night.

Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur wasn't ready to commit to a starting quarterback on Sunday afternoon, even if his backup just led them to a wild overtime win against the Dallas Cowboys.

But just 24 hours after that victory, he made the move. Gardner Minshew is their starter moving forward.

LaFleur opted to bench Jacoby Brissett for Minshew on Sunday afternoon at AT&T Stadium, a decision that eventually led to their 33-30 overtime win against the Cowboys. LaFleur declined to commit to either quarterback when asked directly after the game, even though the expectation was that Minshew would remain in the role.

"I'm just excited about this win right now," he said, via ESPN.

Now, Minshew will get the start against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. Carson Beck will serve as his backup, and Brissett will be the team's third-string quarterback.

The Baltimore Ravens are in need of at least one more quarterback and now have one on their practice squad. They signed Austin Reed to their practice squad on Monday.

All-Pro starter Lamar Jackson left Sunday's loss to the Buffalo Bills with a thumb injury that will require surgery and a stint on injured reserve. It's not yet clear if the injury is season-ending.

Backup Tyler Huntley suffered a toe injury in the same game that sidelined him before halftime. His prognosis was not yet clear as of Monday afternoon. Third-string emergency quarterback Joe Fagnano finished the 36-10 loss for the Ravens. He completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards with an interception and no touchdowns.

Reed, 26, has never thrown an NFL pass. He played two seasons at Western Kentucky in 2022 and 2023 and spent part of training camp this summer with the Ravens.

The Ravens are facing a short with with a Thursday night game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Micah Parsons will be back at Packers practice this week in a significant step in his return from a torn ACL.

Head coach Matt LaFleur announced the news on Monday. It remains unclear when Parsons will make his 2026 season debut.

Parsons tore his left ACL and damaged his meniscus in Week 15 last season against the Denver Broncos on Dec. 14. His return to the field is taking longer than anticipated.

There were reports that Parsons and the Packers were targeting a potential Week 6 return against his former Dallas Cowboys. It's now Week 9.

The Packers are off to a 5-3 start without Parsons, which has them in last place in a competitive NFC North behind the 6-1 Vikings and 5-2 Lions and Bears. The Packers are hoping the eventual return of their All-Pro pass rusher can help propel them to the playoffs.

Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters that quarterback Kyler Murray is dealing with hamstring soreness.

When asked whether Murray's injury could affect his availability for next Monday's game against the Bills, O'Connell said, "I don't think we're there yet."

#2741. ‘Just a lot of waiting going on’: David Benavidez critiques Canelo Alvarez’s performance against Christian Mbilli

Canelo Alvarez came out with a clear win over Christian Mbilli over the weekend, but not everyone thinks so highly of his performance. Speaking to Fight Hub TV, David Benavidez explains why he wasn't impressed by what he saw out of Canelo and believes Canelo owes a better effort to the fans and those who pay him a fortune to fight. Here are some excerpts of what he had to say below.

"He earns all this money, he's supposed to be the greatest fighter in the world, right?" Benavidez said. "We expect him to go in there and knock this guy out. We don't expect him to just go in there and look for counter shots. If the other guy is not throwing any shots, then be Canelo. Go in there, put pressure on, use your defense, use your head movement, go in there — just like how he did it with Caleb Plant…

"So, in my opinion, you're getting $40M, $50M, that's a lot of money. You [should] be ready to push it to the limit every single round, from round one to round 12. And I'm not trying to talk sh-t or nothing, but is that not true? Is that not what you guys see? There's just a lot of waiting going on. As a fighter, Canelo is way better than Mbilli. You guys seen it, he has more tools. It's just that he wasn't pursuing the knockout like he should be.

"I think if you're better than the fighter, you have more skills, put them skills to the test, especially if you're getting money like that. That's just the way I think. I think it was a great performance by him but he just needed to — I don't know, I think he could take all these guys out, could knock them out, especially like Mbilli. Mbilli was fighting scared but you know you're going to get a guy to fight scared — put the pressure on, do some Julio Cesar Chavez and get that knockout.

"He's too much of a good fighter to just be cruising like that, especially earning them top dollars."

#2740. Avalanche sign star Cale Makar to largest contract in NHL history at $163.2 million

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

This has been the summer of spending in the NHL, and the Colorado Avalanche just broke the bank for star defenseman Cale Makar. On Friday, the team announced that Makar signed an eight-year extension worth $163.2 million.

The contract is the richest in league history -- both in total value and annual value at $20.4 million per year. Makar is the first player in NHL history to cross the $20 million salary threshold.

At 27-years old, Makar is arguably the best defensemen in the NHL, and he will remain in that conversation for quite a while. Makar has already won the Norris Trophy twice, and he was a key factor in Colorado's Stanley Cup run, which ended with him winning the Conn Smythe Trophy.

This past season, Makar posted monster numbers from the blue line yet again as he tallied 20 goals and 59 assists in 75 games. Since entering the NHL in 2019, Makar leads all defensemen in goals (20) and points (507).

"I am so excited and humbled to continue to wear the Avalanche sweater and represent this incredible organization and community," Makar said in a statement. "I would like to thank the Kroenke family, Joe Sakic and the entire Avalanche organization for their commitment, trust and belief in me. I would also like to thank my wife and family for their constant support, as well as Scott, Brian and Steve Bartlett for their guidance and assistance.

"To the Avalanche fans, thank you for your continued support and for welcoming us to Colorado years ago. Colorado has truly become a second home to us, and we are so grateful to be here. I look forward to getting back on the ice with my teammates and continuing to work toward our goal of bringing the Stanley Cup back to the Mile High City."

Over the last three seasons, Makar's impact has been immense in all three zones. He's posted a five-on-five expected goals share of 54.5%, per Natural Stat Trick. With Makar on the ice in those situations, Colorado has outscored its opponents 220-157. In two of the last three seasons, Makar has hit the 90-point mark, and he has 100-point potential at his best.

Makar's $11.4 million raise kicks in in at the start of the 2026-27 season, and it will make things significantly tighter for the Avalanche as they navigate the salary cap. The bright side for Colorado -- and the key in getting this deal done -- is that the team now has each of its core players signed through at least 2031.

There may be some sticker shock upon seeing the $20.4 million average annual value, but that's the new reality in the NHL as the cap rises exponentially. The previous record for highest salary in NHL history was just set earlier this offseason when the Anaheim Ducks signed center Leo Carlsson to a contract worth $18 million per year, and the Chicago Blackhawks announced a $75 million extension for Connor Bedard.

The next domino to fall will be an extension for Minnesota Wild defenseman Quinn Hughes, who is neck-and-neck with Makar as the best defensemen in the world. Waiting until after the Makar deal was announced to sign Hughes could prove to be a mistake for Wild general manager Bill Guerin.

#2739. Confirmed lineups: Eintracht Frankfurt vs. Hamburger SV

#2738. Phoenix is falling behind, and there’s no room for another slow start

There are plenty of things in life that give people anxiety. For me, it's being late. Or even the threat of being late. Perhaps it's the military man in me, somebody who made the mistake of showing up late to formation during basic training and paid for it in the front-leaning rest position, beads of sweat dripping off my nose and forming a puddle beneath me on the warm pavement at Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri, one June morning. If you're not early, you're late. That's been my mantra ever since.

Unfortunately, that familiar anxiety is beginning to build regarding the Phoenix Suns. This team is 12th in the Western Conference standings after starting 1-4, something we've seen before. At this point last season, the Suns were also 1-4 and were 13th. The difference then is they were only 3.0 games out of first, and due to an odd scheduling start for the Suns and the fact that they have played the fewest games in the NBA, they are 4.5 games back of the top team in the league. That team? The Rockets…

These slow starts create a significant barrier between the Suns and a proverbial train that's already leaving the station, headed toward the postseason. That's right, the Suns are in danger of being late for that train. Anxiety! Because with every passing day and every loss that accumulates, they find themselves falling further and further behind, making it increasingly difficult to hop on board and reach their desired postseason destination.

A season ago, we found ourselves in the same predicament, but the feeling surrounding the team was much different. A big part of that came down to expectations. Nobody really expected the Suns to be a team that could compete at a high level. The prevailing thought was to let the season play out, sell off assets around the trade deadline, and begin building toward the summer of 2026.

Following that 1-4 start, the Suns began putting things together. The sloppy basketball we'd witnessed early in the season became more organized, and the effort that was evident through those first five games finally started translating into wins. I had this to say after they lost 114-113 to the Grizzlies a season ago:

Losing still stings, but this team isn't miles away. The execution needs tightening, and these are the aches that come with learning how to win again.

It's tough to find moral victories in Game 5 when you're sitting at 1–4, but I'll say it anyway. I was entertained. Disappointed, sure. The ending wasn't what anyone wanted. But maybe this year isn't about wins and losses. Maybe it's about how they respond to nights like this.

The feeling this year is different, however. Locally, expectations were higher, even if the national perception remained relatively unchanged. The roster construction was clunky, but you could at least see the vision of what this team wanted to become. Regardless, those expectations change the reality of your situation. While the effort has certainly been present, its consistency has begun to wane, and the execution remains frustratingly inconsistent.

Last season, we could talk ourselves into believing thatDillon Brooks and Jalen Green's absence due to injury was a significant reason for the team's struggles. And perhaps this year, we're doing the same thing with Mark Williams. But the feeling isn't the same. The reality of the situation is slowly sinking in, and it's one in which hope is becoming increasingly difficult to find. This is a team that doesn't control its own draft picks, so finding itself stuck in the middle of the standings is essentially a death sentence.

When you consider the anti-tanking rules that will be in place this year, there's a very real possibility that the Suns could find themselves among the teams with an 8.1% chance of landing the number one overall pick. And how "Suns" would it be for Phoenix to benefit from not being completely horrendous under the league's new draft lottery structure, only to have to hand that pick over to Houston?

Are we there yet? Are we seriously thinking about this already? (I am) When you start 1-4 and look around the standings at the other teams with only one win, seeing the Kings, Nets, Jazz, Bulls, and Bucks alongside you, it's difficult not to get a little frazzled. Because those are the teams that were projected to be bad. It's why we're running to the trade machine trying to find fixes, because you have no room for a down season when there is no benefit to being bad.

I think back to a season ago and the turnaround we witnessed. What the Suns accomplished was impressive, climbing out of 13th place in the Western Conference and playing some incredibly good basketball along the way. For one fleeting night on January 22, 2026, the Suns had fought their way all the way back to the fifth seed in the Western Conference. After starting 1-4, they went 26-13 to reach that point. That is going to be incredibly hard to replicate.

Can this team reproduce any aspect of what we witnessed last year? Can they put together another impressive run that allows them to hop aboard that train headed toward the postseason?

There is hope if you look hard enough. Through their first 5 games a season ago, the Suns had a 120.5 defensive rating (28th) and -9.8 net rating (27th). This season, they are at 124.0 (30th) and -9.8 (25th). After their 1-4 start a season ago, the Suns posted a 112.3 defensive rating (8th) and a +2.1 net rating (13th). It is possible. We've seen it before.

Psst…I'm saying the quiet part out loud…that team can rebound the damn ball…the worst team in rebound percentage last season was the Washington Wizards at 47.1%. The Suns are currently at 45.7%…

We've got a long trip ahead of us, my fellow Suns fans, and we'll spend much of that journey wondering whether this team can recapture any semblance of what it was a season ago. We'll look for solutions in every corner, talking ourselves into the viability of overpaid players like Domantas Sabonis or Dejounte Murray as mediocre saviors. But with so many red flags surrounding the roster construction, it's difficult to shake that familiar feeling of anxiety from being late building in the pit of your stomach.

#2737. Eagles waive player they traded for last year

The Philadelphia Eagles are waiving Jakorian Bennett, as noted by the NFL's November 3 personnel notice.

The Eagles previously opened Bennett's 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve on October 14. The team was coming up on the deadline to either 1) activate him to the roster or 2) shut him down for the remainder of the 2026 season.

Instead, the Eagles chose door No. 3 and waived him from IR to apparently allow him to catch on with a new team. Or perhaps he could return to Philly on the practice squad if he does land elsewhere?

Finding themselves in need of corner help, the Eagles originally acquired Bennett in a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders last summer. There was hope the 2023 fourth-round pick might be able to contribute but he ended up logging just 98 defensive snaps (69 of which came in Week 18 last year with the Eagles resting starters) and 58 defensive snaps in 2025.

Bennett began the 2026 season on IR after getting injured in the preseason. Had he stayed healthy, he might've pushed for the top backup outside cornerback role that has instead been claimed by veteran Jonathan Jones. But with Jones recently getting hurt and being a 33-year-old playing on a one-year deal, it could've made sense to put Bennett in that role instead. He could've even been in line to see starting snaps with the Eagles potentially set to move Riq Woolen ahead of the NFL trade deadline.

Meanwhile, the Raiders are still utilizing Thomas Booker IV, whom the Eagles gave up to get Bennett. Booker logged the third-most defensive tackle snaps for Las Vegas last year and the fourth-most so far this season.

The Eagles also released wide receiver Quentin Skinner from the practice squad after originally signing him last week.

#2736. How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker

CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he's a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State.

Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California.

He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years.

"I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today," Comer said.

He had 58 tackles (8.5 for loss), including six sacks at the California junior college and got on the radar of linebackers coach Cort Dennison, then at Idaho. Dennison kept pursuing Comer at OSU, where he signed in January and arrived during the spring.

Justin Joyner wins first game as Oregon State coach in blowout

Atkinson, Legree join Nike's Blue Ribbon Elite as OSU extends apparel deal

Pac-12 confirms play clock error led to penalty on Oregon State in its loss to Fresno State

At 6-foot-4 and 245 pounds, Comer was dominating in junior college from his athleticism alone. He didn't know the finer points of playing football. Hand placement, setting the edge in the run game and pass coverage were not in his repertoire. Comer was there to pin his ears back and attack the quarterback, regardless of the down and distance.

"They didn't ask much of me," Comer said. "They told me just do what I do, use my athleticism, get to the quarterback."

What Comer lacks in experience, he makes up for in ability. He consistently ranks among OSU's fastest players in practice, which was invaluable to a team seeking more pass rush.

"His athleticism is off the charts," defensive coordinator Mike MacIntyre said. "We see him grow leaps and bounds. Playing a lot more (against Montana), he will grow leaps and bounds going into this Saturday because now he's seen it, it slows down, he understands the different things."

RELATED: Experts release Oregon State vs. UTEP predictions, best bets, and preview for Week 4

Comer has 10 tackles thus far, including four in each of the past two games, and is already more than a situational pass rusher for the Beavers. He credits MacIntyre and edge coaches Joe Seumalo and George Frazier with helping him learn the game, particularly pass coverage.

Ideally, pairing Comer with Takari Hickle will allow OSU to generate more pressure as teams won't be able to focus all their offensive line on one side.

"Teams have to respect his speed," Hickle said. "If they don't, then he'll run right by them. He is definitely a threat in coverage and in the pass game."

#2735. 2026 NHL free agent tracker: Patrick Kane returns to Blackhawks on two-year contract

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

NHL free agency has slowed down in late July, but some notable names are still coming off the board. Most notably, Patrick Kane is returning to the Chicago Blackhawks on a two-year contract worth $16 million, the team announced on Thursday.

Already a Chicago legend and future Hall of Famer, Kane won three Stanley Cups and a slew of individual awards with the franchise that selected him with the No. 1 overall pick in 2007. Kane's first stint with the Blackhawks lasted 16 seasons, and he piled up 446 goals and 779 assists in 1,161 games. Kane ranks inside the top five of just about every statistical category in franchise history, and he will get the chance to keep climbing those lists over the next two years.

The Blackhawks sent Kane to the New York Rangers at the 2023 NHL trade deadline, and he played just 19 regular season games there before hitting free agency the next summer. Hip surgery delayed Kane's decision until November of that year, but he ultimately landed with the Detroit Red Wings, where he's spent the last three seasons.

Last season was Kane's best with Detroit, and it proved that he still had some gas left in the tank, at least offensively. Kane posted 16 goals and 41 assists in 67 games -- with 19 of those points coming on the power play.

In his second stint with the Blackhawks, Kane will add another level of playmaking to the power play, and he should strengthen a top six forward group that's bereft of proven talent. Kane will also be an excellent mentor and sounding board for fellow No. 1 overall pick, Connor Bedard, who is set to miss the first month of the season after undergoing shoulder surgery.

Kane isn't the player he once was, but he'll give Chicago a bit more pop at the top of the lineup, and his first game back in a Blackhawks jersey will be a huge night for the city.

#2732. 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State

FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children's Stadium.

Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State.

Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching.

The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn't diminish what's being accomplished this season. They're simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now.

JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season.

Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State's tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter.

Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle's would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton's foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn't occur.

That doesn't even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits.

Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that's to be expected. Oregon State's offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU's rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it's not a particularly stout group.

Fresno State's 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. If there's one piece OSU's receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why.

OSU showed a vulnerability early, but against Houston and Texas Tech it was understandable in terms of talent and timing on the schedule.

Tackling improved over the prior five games, but opponents' speed also dropped. Against legitimate athletic threats, the Beavers showed their tackling fundamentals, speed, strength and angles are still areas of weakness.

Entz detailed Atkinson's reliance on his first read and susceptibility to being impacted by pass rush when it's not there. Of course, a defense has to have the talent and ability to do something about it. Atkinson's ceiling is high provided he develops in his reading of progressions, grows more comfortable checking into run plays and finds effective counters to the better defenses OSU faces.

Ojeda's three field goals should not get lost to the box score, particularly with a 54-yarder.

At 14-9, if OSU manages to make a stop and gain momentum, the game could have changed and the importance of Ojeda's kicks becomes paramount to the game.

As the sample size for OSU's kickoffs grows, so too does the success opponents continue to have. To allow a 44-yard kickoff return following a 14-play drive that spanned more than five minutes is inexcusable. OSU would literally have been better off kicking out of bounds, which has been enough of an issue as well.

The Beavers rank 114th in average kickoff return yards allowed and 126th on a per game basis.

Without belaboring a point that's been stated on nearly a weekly basis, the matchup disadvantage at No. 2 corner remains the Achilles' heel for the defense.

Against bigger receivers like Freeman it's simply a matter of when, not if, they will haul in big catches.

#2731. What We Learned from the Spurs win over the Jazz

Somewhere in the second quarter, with the Spurs up one and about to be up more, I realized I wasn't watching the game. I was, instead, watching myself not watch the game, which is a worse hobby and the one I'm apparently best at. The game was fine. The game was exactly what it said on the label: a nondescript tilt between two teams already headed down different tracks. The shine of October basketball had worn off completely and, like summer turning to fall, the Grind had arrived.

As a first quarter blowout turned into a 2nd quarter snoozer, my brain began to wander a bit. I could be anywhere in the world right now. A plastic stool in Hanoi, a bowl of pho, a little light rain. A mountain pass in the Andes, thin air, nobody asking me for a take. Man, I should be reading books. Seeing films. I should be the kind of person whose passport has all those cool stamps in it. This one precious life the universe handed me was unraveling in real time as Ace Bailey stepped into a 25-foot pull-up three to cut the Jazz's deficit to one.

Then Stephon Castle missed a layup and I almost decided to call it a night. It was as annoying as it was unremarkable and I just didn't need it anymore. I reached for the remote and, as I did, Victor Wembanyama, who a minute earlier had similarly flubbed an alley-oop, grabbed the rebound and tipped it back in. Twenty seconds after Bailey's three. No celebration. Barely a facial expression.

I'd love to tell you that's the moment I'd been looking for, but that would be too tidy. What I'd been searching for was a hook. A story, a cause, a catalyst. Anything to hold off the particular ennui of being a fan of a good team. And Wemby wasn't even good last night, not by any stretch. Five of fifteen. Zero for five from three. Five turnovers. He was in that mode he gets in from time to time where he decides the Key to Victory is to simply chuck it.

The Spurs won by 22 anyway, not because of a miracle but because this roster has more than one way to be competent. The Spurs are, mercifully, more than the sum of their parts.

Not that the parts are bad. Quite the contrary. Dylan Harper scored all 17 of his points before the third quarter was half over. Stephon Castle is an animal. De'Aaron Fox looks like the guy we paid for. Tarris Reed continues to grab rebounds in a way that feels like it's going to be important (seven in about seven minutes last night). Every wing combination we've thrown on the court is its own kind of fun.

I mean, look at Harrison Barnes. A man as old as time itself (he's four years younger than me) had an insanely active night. He knocked down threes from 29, 25 and 24 feet, he ran around, he caused trouble. Early in the fourth he got tangled up with Brice Sensabaugh, slid across the floor, got back up, and just stared at him while the refs reviewed it in slow motion. I'm told that clip racked up 140,000 views on the world wide web within about an hour.

The thing about the Grind is that it doesn't have to mean anything, which means that everything within the Grind gets to be exactly what it is. A tip dunk. A well executed outlet pass. An old man staring down Brice Sensabaugh. Like, I didn't come out of the womb craving the Larry O'Brien trophy. I just was at my breakfast table in 1996 watching Michael Jordan dunk on Rik Smits during a SportsCenter rerun, and some part of me said, with zero strategic vision, "Yes. More of that." More of that was the entire ask and, frankly, it still is.

Look at us. You and me. Like I said, we could be anywhere in the world right now, but we're right here with the Spurs and the Jazz on a Monday night in November. The stools in Hanoi will still be there someday, but a precocious superstar, having the worst night of his season, is putting a ball back through the hoop like a child tucking in his stuffed animals for the night.

You don't have to impress some greater importance on a moment like that to make it mean something. You were there. It's a part of you now and you got to live it.

If that isn't special, I don't know what is.

Dylan Harper seems almost casually good at basketball. It's remarkable and breathtaking, these things he's doing, but it also has that effect of seeming effortless when he's casually dismantling another team. In the second quarter he stole the ball and in a blink Vassell was dunking off his pass. In the third, he stole it again and Stephon was finishing an alley-oop before I'd even registered it. He added 8 assists and 7 rebounds on top of all his scoring. I find myself almost taking it for granted at this point, and we've really only started to scratch the surface of what he's capable of. Scary to think about! (For our opponents. For us it's just exceedingly cool and fun.)

I know it's just the Jazz, grain of salt and all that, but I never get tired of seeing the Spurs get out on the break and run. They won fast-break points 26-9, against a Jazz team that turned it over just 11 times, a season low for Utah, so a lot of that was pure rebound-and-go. They also won the paint 52-36 and opened the game on an 18-2 run. Run for days my boys. Grab the ball and never stop running. Only good can come from this. Open looks from three, easy paths to the rim, potential foul trouble for the opponents. Push that pace. Push that pace. PUSH THAT PACE.

This is not how development works and, to be clear, I don't know what I'm talking about, but I absolutely crave Tarris Reed minutes. I want him to become a Sasquatch, Godzilla, King Kong, Loch Ness, Goblin, ghoul and a zombie with no conscience. I want basketballs to fear him checking into the game because they're about to get rebounded to within an inch of their lives.

I love a wire-to-wire win. Next time you hear me complaing about a wire to wire win feel free to come to my house and take an ice cold waterloo out of my fridge as payment for my sins.

I'm a man of all seasons, to be clear, but right now, yes, I am currently in a Waterloo phase of my Sparkling Water career.

There is a particular Black Cherry flavor I've grown fond of and I just can't stay away at this point. It scratches this weird nostalgic part of my brain that yearns for a Blue Sky soda I had in my youth. Do you remember Blue Sky soda?

Yeah, the cans were cool. I don't know. I think I had just never experienced the concept of a soda that existed outside the mainstream world of the Coca-Cola and Pepsi family trees, so when I went on vacation and saw this crazy looking can with a cherry sitting on a cloud it just… broke my brain a little bit and I had to have it.

Who could say? I was six years old. I'd left the summer heat in Texas and woken up the next day in a Colorado mountain town sipping an alien soda from heaven. Maybe it was good, maybe it wasn't, but it stirred something deep in my soul that I think I've been searching for ever since.

And Black Cherry Waterloos scratch that itch for you?

They do. Publix also pretty regularly throws them in Buy One Get Ones for me and who am I to turn down a deal like that.

#2730. 2026-27 NHL season predictions: Expert picks for Stanley Cup playoffs, champion and major awards this season

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Following a brief offseason and an expedited preseason, the 2026-27 NHL season has arrived. Before the puck drops on opening night, we have some predictions to make.

If this season feel like it's staring earlier than usual, that's because it is. The NHL is adopting an 84-game regular season, which just means more hockey for the rest of us. That also means a long and arduous journey to the Stanley Cup is ever so slightly more difficult.

So, what will that journey look like? The Carolina Hurricanes are looking to defend their title as Cup champions, but they'll have to contend with a deep Eastern Conference and some real juggernauts in the Western Conference. With that in mind, we logged our expert predictions for the playoff field in each conference -- and there were a few surprises -- before making our Stanley Cup Final selections.

We also called our shot on the winners of each major individual award. Connor McDavid is looking for his fourth Hart Trophy, but he's got some competition from an up-and-coming superstar in his own division. Races for the Norris Trophy and Vezina Trophy should be pretty wide open, and unexpected candidates always emerge throughout the season.

It should be a fun season in the NHL, so follow along with all our coverage at CBS Sports. Let's get things kicked off with the season preview and predictions, which will of course be 100% accurate.

Baumgartner: I don't see many new faces entering the conversation when it comes to the Eastern Conference playoff race. A healthy Florida Panthers side will slot themselves right back towards the top of the Atlantic, and a revamped Washington Capitals side should be able to make some noise in the Metropolitan. Besides that, I have six 2026 playoff teams returning to the dance in 2027.

Nivison: As much as I hate to go with chalk in preseason predictions -- because it rarely happens that way -- there's no denying the top dogs in the West. The Avalanche and Stars are the class of the Central Division, and the Golden Knights should pound a pitiful Pacific Division into a pulp. Things get more interesting behind those clear Cup contenders, and I'm projecting another significant leap forward from the Mammoth. I also think Macklin Celebrini will be successful in dragging the Sharks to the playoffs in his third NHL season.

Nivison -- Columbus Blue Jackets: The Blue Jackets have been agonizingly close to the playoffs in each of the last two seasons, and I think they get over the hump in 2026-27. There are still questions in Columbus. Can Adam Fantilli be a franchise player at center? Is the forward group as a whole good enough to keep pace in a competitive Eastern Conference? Still, I am sure the Blue Jackets have a really strong blue line, led by Norris Trophy winner Zach Werenski, and goaltender Jet Greaves is on track to become a Vezina Trophy candidate. Internal improvements from the young core will then get Columbus above the cut line.

Baumgartner -- San Jose Sharks: The Sharks narrowly missed out on the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, finishing just four points short of the second wild card. San Jose added a good group of veterans over the summer, but the most important offseason move was selecting Ivar Stenberg with the No. 2 pick in the Draft. Stenberg joins the youth movement in San Jose, which is spearheaded by new captain Macklin Celebrini, who broke the Sharks single-season points record with 115 last season. The Sharks are a better team than they were last year, and with Celebrini entering his third season as a legit Hart Trophy contender, this team won't be fun to play against.

Nivison: Yes, the Mammoth have a brutal path coming out of the Central Divison, but just close your eyes and imagine this scenario with me. Logan Cooley becomes a superstar center. Dylan Guenther hits 50 goals. Dmitry Simashev asserts himself as a budding top-four defenseman. Anders Lee and Vincent Trocheck provide necessary veteran depth. Now open your eyes. Utah is your Western Conference champion.

Unfortunately for the Mammoth, they will run into a refreshed Panthers team that now has double-barreled Tkachuks. Last season, we found out that all it takes to stop Florida is to hope all of its key players miss significant time with injury. The long offseason was probably a blessing in disguise as it allowed the Panthers to get healthy, and that's bad news for everyone else. The structure in front of the crease will limit some of the volatility we saw from Jacob Markstrom in New Jersey, and Florida wins its third Stanley Cup in four years.

Baumgartner: Before last season, the Carolina Hurricanes' kryptonite was the Eastern Conference Final. The Hurricanes were able to overcome their demons and win the East before ultimately taking home the franchise's first Stanley Cup since 2006. In the West, the Dallas Stars have been running into the same problem. After three straight seasons ending in the Western Conference Final, the Stars regressed last postseason, flaming out in the first-round to the Minnesota Wild. The Central Division will once again be a gauntlet, but I'm ready for Dallas to take the next step and reach the Stanley Cup Final.

While Dallas has continued to fall short in recent years, the Panthers have done the opposite. The Panthers made three consecutive Stanley Cup Final appearances, winning back-to-back Cups in 2023-24 and 2024-25. Last season, Florida's three-peat attempt came to a halt on day one of training after captain Aleksander Barkov went down with a non-contact injury, tearing both the ACL and MCL in his right knee. An offseason of healing for Barkov, and the rest of the banged up Panthers, has the team refreshed entering September for the first time in years. With nearly the entire 2025 Stanley Cup winning core still on the team and Brady Tkachuk added to the fold, Florida looks ready to win its third Stanley Cup in four seasons.

Nivison: Celebrini should have won the Hart Trophy last season, but for some incomprehensible reason, he wasn't even a finalist. This year, Celebrini replicates that performance and gets San Jose to the postseason to take home his first MVP award at age 20. Hughes posts a career year in his first full season with the Wild, and Spencer Carberry gets his flowers for winning the Metro Division after missing the playoffs last year.

Baumgartner: McDavid's ability to take over a game was evident nearly every time he touched the ice last season. His 24 points (11 goals,13 assists) in the final 14 games of the regular season -- without Leon Draisaitl in the lineup -- was one of the many reasons I put him No. 1 on my Hart Trophy ballot. With just two years left on his current contract, desperation may start to kick in to get the job in Edmonton, which would lead to another MVP-caliber season. Barkov is healthy and the frontrunner to win his fourth Selke, and Dahlin will have another strong season to take home his first career Norris Trophy.

#2729. Everybody is talking about Bears making Khalil Mack trade. Here’s who they must get instead

Everybody is talking about Bears making Khalil Mack trade. Here's who they must get instead appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Chicago Bears have a quarterback on a roll. And they made Jeffery Simmons a very happy man. But they might still need another piece to help with their Super Bowl assault. And while everybody is talking about the Bears making a Khalil Mack trade, here is who they must get instead.

Mack, an edge rusher, would certainly add value to the Bears' defense. However, the Bears, as they stand now, rank No. 6 in the NFL with 22 sacks. And that's mostly without Simmons creating problems in the middle that can help things on the outside.

And Bears GM Ryan Poles might be better served to add a player at the cornerback position.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

There has been talk of the Bears going after Tariq Woolen. The Eagles cornerback is having a strong season. And it makes sense, in one way, to trade for a player who has good numbers on his side.

However, the Bears don't want to give up too much. This is a young roster that could be competitive for the next 3-4 years. Draft picks are valuable. And the Eagles will want a pretty penny for Woolen. Plus, Woolen's play has trailed off some in recent seasons. And he doesn't have a pick in eight games with six passes defended.

But the best route is Jackson. He has been a solid starter in his NFL career with the Panthers, Steelers, and the last two years with the Chargers. This year, he's played in four games with limited success. Still, Jackson brings positive things to the table, according to ESPN.

"With his backfield vision and short-area closing speed, Jackson fits best as a zone corner," Matt Bowen wrote. "He's a top-down defender with route awareness who can create on-the-ball production. Jackson has 23 interceptions and 68 pass breakups over his career."

Those interceptions are an important part of the package. He had nine picks over the 2024 and 2025 seasons. The Bears would love a playmaker in the secondary. They have a middle-of-the-pack five interceptions so far this year.

And Jackson profiles well against the run. He has a Pro Football Focus grade of 77.5 this year in a limited sample size. However, he graded out at 72.9 back in 2024.

And Jackson brings a confident approach to the field, according to Chargers.com.

"I feel like the last two seasons I've emerged, to me personally, as one of the top corners in the league," Jackson said before the season. "That's just kind of how I feel, so just adding to that."

"I'm team first, so I don't have a personal agenda," Jackson said. "I don't have any personal goals but to be the best teammate I could be. Just blessed to have a group of guys that share that same mindset. Nobody is selfish. Nobody has selfish goals."

Jackson would be a good fit for the Bears' tough mindset on the defensive side of the ball.

It doesn't help cornerback Jaylon Johnson's case that he hasn't played well this season. That's especially true with the two-time Pro Bowler's tackling woes, according to Heavy.com via Yahoo.

"There's nothing that I can say as far as an excuse, a rhyme or reason," Johnson said. "I've just got to get it done."

The Bears also have Tyrique Stevenson Sr. at a starting cornerback position. But he hasn't played well, either.

The team is hoping Coby Bryant can return from preseason surgery before the season is over, but there are no guarantees for that to happen as he tries to work his way back. The safety would help the secondary and thus take some pressure off Johnson and Stevenson.

Dalen Terry is on an NBA roster after starting the season on the sidelines.

#2722. Rockets top NBA power rankings for the week

The Houston Rockets are off to a red-hot start, leading the NBA with a 7-1 record, as well as holding wins over the Boston Celtics, Oklahoma City Thunder, and San Antonio Spurs. The team has looked like the same hard-nosed defensive team we have grown used to, but this time with some idea of an offensive plan. In addition, the team is playing within the flow of the offense, not forcing things to Alperen Sengun or Kevin Durant, with the "Stand Around and Watch KD" offense of last year showing less and less of itself. Marcus Smart has been a solid addition so far, and Jabari Smith Jr. seems poised for a career year.

Granted, it's early in the season, but the Rockets look good right now, and it seems some others might agree. The Athletic released it's new series of NBA power rankings, and low and behold, who sits atop at the moment but your Houston Rockets. Here's what they had to say about our boys:

Last ranking: FourthIn the last week: W vs ATL, W at MIL, L at DAL, W vs OKCOffensive rating: 121.2 (first place)Defensive rating: 108.9 (ninth place)

Starters: Fred VanVleet, Amen Thompson, Kevin Durant, Jabari Smith Jr., Alperen ŞengünKey reserves: Marcus Smart, Tari Eason, Reed Sheppard, Clint Capela, Bogdan Bogdanović

Houston's improved depth hasn't quite made the defense special, which makes sense. The Rockets don't have great rim protection, they have a small guard in the starting lineup and their best player is 38. The Rockets tried to get away with lineups without centers in Dallas with Şengün nursing a back injury, and it's one reason they aren't undefeated anymore. But this offense has taken off, and Houston is deeper than it has been at any point under coach Ime Udoka.

So with the Rockets cruising, the Thunder hurt and the Spurs off to an up-and-down start, it's your Rockets who are currently playing the best ball in the NBA. Right behind Houston are the 5-1 Detroit Pistons and the 6-1 Philadelphia LeBrons. I think the Rockets are better than either of those teams, but time will tell. For now, enjoy the the early-season success.

#2718. Raphinha, Yamal power Barca to Champions League win over Villa

Raphinha struck twice to propel Barcelona to a 3-0 Champions League win over visitors Aston Villa on Tuesday, ending the English side's perfect start to the competition.

Five-time winners Barcelona took an early lead through Lamine Yamal before Raphinha continued his fine goalscoring form with a second-half brace.

Barca bounced back after defeat by champions Paris Saint-Germain in their previous European outing to stay in the hunt for a top eight league phase berth.

Unai Emery's Villa competed well in the first half but were eventually undone by Barca's greater ability in the final third.

The Champions League anthem was not played before the game, as a mark of respect for Tenerife striker Jesus De Miguel, who died on Tuesday morning after an on-pitch collision in a Spanish second division match the previous day, provoking shock across the football world.

"Yes it was (a good win), I want to dedicate this win to the fans, but today I don't want to talk about football, I want to send a message to the family of Jesus -- may he rest in peace," Raphinha told Movistar.

"This can happen to anyone, it's very tough... you're going to play a game and the same thing can happen to you...

"From the club, I want to send a message of strength to the family."

Villa captain John McGinn had only visited the Camp Nou once previously, on a summer holiday as an eight-year-old, and might have expected better weather than the downpour both teams were subjected to.

The skipper might also have expected a more focused start, with Villa handing Barcelona the lead in the seventh minute.

The Spanish champions pressed Aston Villa extremely high and Joao Gomes played a poor pass straight to Yamal in his own box. The 19-year-old winger gladly took the gift and stroked past Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki.

"Tonight was a huge learning curve for us and I am sure it will stand us in good stead for the future," McGinn told TNT Sports.

"Barcelona made the right decisions at the right times and scored really good goals."

Yamal's goal was his 14th in the competition across his career, beating Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe's previous record tally of 13 netted as a teenager in the Champions League.

Emery, who endured one of the worst nights of his career away at Barca when helming PSG in 2017 during a 6-1 defeat, may have feared the worst.

However Villa reacted strongly and Matty Cash had a vicious drive deflected narrowly wide before Joao Cancelo blocked Gomes's effort.

Barcelona goalkeeper Joan Garcia was quick off his line to beat Nicolas Jackson to a dangerous through-ball.

Suzuki saved from Anthony Gordon as Villa again struggled to bring the ball out from the back under Barca's pressing.

Garcia was called into action again by Johan Manzambi as the match lurched from end-to-end.

Barcelona extended their lead early in the second half when Fermin Lopez fed Raphinha, who showed quick footwork before finding the bottom corner.

Cancelo set up Raphinha for Barcelona's third with a superb cross with the outside of his boot. The Brazil winger, who has made the number nine position his own this season, pounced from close range for his 19th goal across all competitions.

"He's in a good moment," said Flick. "I'm really happy with him, he's an amazing player."

Yamal sent a shot skidding wide as Barcelona probed for a fourth. It did not come, but the Catalan giants were able to record a first Champions League clean sheet in 19 games.

Barcelona visit Atletico Madrid in La Liga on Sunday and will be waiting to see if midfielder Rodri Hernandez is fit to play.

The former Manchester City star was replaced at half-time by Marc Bernal and Flick said Rodri had felt some muscular "discomfort".

Flick was pleased with Barcelona keeping Villa at bay.

"It was important that we defended together very compactly," said the German coach.

"The back line played on an amazing level, they defended everything."

#2715. Demichelis vows to leave RB Leipzig if season targets aren't met

Martin Demichelis has had an inconsistent start as RB Leipzig head coach since replacing Ole Werner in the summer, with several heavy defeats away from home putting him under considerable pressure.

Saturday’s 2-0 win over Schalke 04 at the Veltins-Arena finally delivered Leipzig’s first away league victory of the season, with Demichelis using the occasion to make his position on the club’s expectations clear.

“I know that I have to achieve targets with RB Leipzig; that’s why I’m here. And if we don’t achieve those targets by the end of the season, then I’ll leave myself. That’s how it is. The people who know me know that very well,” Demichelis was quoted as saying by Bild.

While the club’s exact objectives remain unclear, qualifying for the Champions League is likely to be among the key targets.

Saturday’s win should ease some of the pressure on Demichelis, with Leipzig now sitting fourth in the Bundesliga table.

Nevertheless, the Argentine coach was quick to stress that there is still a long way to go this season.

“It was only our first away win. The season is still a long one,” he said.

#2713. Jake Paul to face former kickboxing champion Cédric Doumbé in Dubai on Christmas Eve

DUBAI — Jake Paul has his opponent for the return. Most Valuable Promotions announced Monday that Paul will face former two-time Glory world champion Cédric Doumbé on Dec. 24 at Coca-Cola Arena in Dubai, ending a year away from the ring after the broken jaw he suffered against Anthony Joshua last December.

The bout is a professionally sanctioned eight-round cruiserweight fight at 200 pounds with 10-ounce gloves. It will be Paul's first fight since Joshua stopped him in the sixth round, a loss that led to jaw surgeries in December and February and left his boxing future in question.

Paul (12-2, 7 KOs) came out swinging in the announcement. He cracked a joke at Doumbé's expense with a nickname, admitted he is rusty and that his jaw is not what it was, then reminded the Frenchman that kickboxing titles do not carry over to a boxing ring. Doumbé was ready with a reply. "I'm going to finish the job Joshua started," he said.

Dec 19, 2025; Miami, Florida, UNITED STATES; Jake Paul is knocked down by Anthony Joshua during a heavyweight boxing bout at Kaseya Center. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images

Sam Navarro-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect

Dec 19, 2025; Miami, Florida, UNITED STATES; Jake Paul is knocked down by Anthony Joshua during a heavyweight boxing bout at Kaseya Center. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images

Doumbé, 34, is one of the most recognizable fighters in French combat sports. He holds a 75-7-1 record in kickboxing with 45 knockouts and is 6-1 in mixed martial arts, including the nine-second knockout of Jordan Zébo for PFL in September 2023 that Paul referenced in his statement. His lone professional boxing appearance was a win in April 2015. MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian said Doumbé has wanted this fight for years and that the timing makes sense.

The announcement comes after several names tried to get in on the date. Hartford's Richard "Popeye The Sailor Man" Rivera (27-3, 20 KOs), a former Paul sparring partner, sent out a release Friday demanding the fight. Darren Till said Monday on The Ariel Helwani Show that Paul's team approached him first, that the sides had talked money and that he had been in camp for two weeks before he found out about Doumbé along with everyone else. Till called the matchup a farce and accused Paul and Bidarian of wasting his time, but said he still wants Paul and believes it could happen next year.

Paul and Doumbé are scheduled to appear at public news conferences Nov. 10 in Paris and Nov. 12 in Dubai.

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2710. Bears vs. Seahawks Game Balls: The Nation Takes Notice

The Chicago Bears can win a Super Bowl. This year. The team left no doubt about that fact on Monday night at Seattle's Lumen Field.

The Bears thoroughly dominated the defending Super Bowl champions, in their own house, from bell to bell. This happening just one week after defeating last year's Super Bowl runner-up New Englad Patriots.

Also one week ago, the Seahawks defense kept Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs out of the end zone entirely. This week, the Bears went on a methodical, 17-play drive to score a touchdown on their first possession of the game against that same defense.

In defeating the Seahawks, as well as the Patriots last week, the Bears became the first team in NFL history to defeat both of the previous year's Super Bowl teams in back-to-back weeks. That's a heck of a stat.

Despite most of the NFL world now acknowledging the fact that Williams is a top tier quarterback, it feels like Monday night's game took that one step further. As I browse social media and the usual talking heads throughout the sports world, I'm starting to see a general consensus now that not only is #18 top-tier, he is elite. As in, a top five quarterback in the league.

A Chicago Bears quarterback. Elite. We've been waiting a long time for this, and we absolutely deserve it.

Williams did something to the Seahawks that no other QB has done this year – throw for 200 yards. And the Seahawks have played some pretty accomplished QBs and big names this year: Mahomes, Brock Purdy, Drake Maye, Justin Herbert, and Bo Nix to name a few. None of them accomplished this feat.

It took Williams barely half the game, surpassing 200 yards less than five minutes into the third quarter. And he did so on one of the most spectacular plays of the game.

The Bears' QB finished the night 24/34, 247 yards passing, one touchdown, zero interceptions, and a passer rating of 101.0.

You've got to think the Williams has firmly entered the MVP discussion and will remain there for the rest of the season.

Did the Bears give up too much for Simmons? If I'm the Titans, I'm thinking they didn't give up enough.

It can't be overstated how much of a difference Big Jeff made for the Bears defense from the very first play he was on the field. Those bright orange sleeves might as well have been a flashing warning sign to the rest of the league for the remainder of this season. Not only do the Bears have an elite offense; they now have a defense that opposing teams will (and should) fear.

That's a combination that wins championships.

In commanding so much attention from the offensive line, Simmons helped other Bears defenders in the front four look like All Pro candidates. Montez Sweat was a beast. Austin Booker continued to look the part of up and coming young star. Hell, James Lynch even had an interception, catching a ball that Booker tipped late in the game.

Simmons was on the field for 48 plays, and the Seahawks were held to just 3.0 yards per play (including three sacks and an interception) during those snaps. There were eight plays that Simmons was not on the field, and Seattle averaged 13.3 yards per play during those snaps. That kind of says it all.

Simmons finished the night with six tackles, one sack, two tackles for loss, one pass defended, and one QB hit.

And this is just the beginning. Simmons had only been with the team for a little bit over 72 hours on Monday night. Expect this train to keep rolling ahead at full speed in the week's ahead.

It hasn't been this exciting to be a Bears fan in a very long time. Relish it.

Who would have received your game balls? Let us know in the comments section below.

The best team in the NFL resides in Chicago.

#2708. 24-year-old runner Rachel Apa dies after collapsing during NYC Marathon

Rachel Apa, a 24-year-old runner in the New York City Marathon, died Sunday night after collapsing in Central Park about two miles from the finish line, according to her family.

Her father, Stephen Apa, said he had been texting his daughter during the race and that she appeared to be doing well earlier on the course.

"After her nine miles, she said she was doing great. I told her, ' Don't overdo it. It's your first marathon," he said.

Stephen Apa spoke by phone from the family's home in Lewiston, Pennsylvania. He said his daughter, a former Division I field hockey player at Bucknell University, continued texting him during the race before she collapsed.

"And then 24 and she didn't text me back at all at any of those, and I just wanted to give her pings so she knew I was still there, you know, watching," he said.

Recalling their final exchange, he said, "She texted me right before 18 and said UGG."

He said that shortly afterward, she texted "ow, ow."

"After that she texted ow, ow. I said go easy, and she said 'ow,' and I said go easy," he said.

It was the last time he heard from his oldest child and only daughter.

Michaela Nicholas, 28, said she and her fiancé were cheering for runners when they saw Apa collapse.

"After she passed by about 5 yards ahead of us, I saw her collapse on the ground," Nicholas said.

"My fiancé immediately screamed for help, screamed for a doctor across the way and I ran to Rachel," she said.

Nicholas said a runner called 911 while doctors in the crowd rushed to Apa and began CPR after finding no pulse.

"I got down next to her and held her hand and I told her that she was loved and wasn't alone," Nicholas said.

Apa's mother, who was waiting for her at mile 25, arrived as an ambulance transported her to Mount Sinai Hospital.

According to her family, Apa worked as a product manager and had recently begun pursuing a master's degree in business. She was running the marathon to raise money in honor of her grandfather, who died from Parkinson's disease.

Stephen Apa said doctors told him his daughter may have collapsed because of a rare muscle condition that can be triggered by exertion.

Jennifer Miao of the ABC News Medical Unit said rhabdomyolysis can affect marathon runners and others engaged in intense physical activity.

"Rhabdo can occur in anybody as young as someone in their 20s that's training for a marathon," Miao said.

As he reflected on his daughter's death, Stephen Apa shared a brief message.

New York Road Runners, which organizes the TCS New York City Marathon, issued a statement saying: "We are deeply saddened by Rachel's passing. Our thoughts and sincere sympathies are with her family, friends, and the entire running community."

#2706. Fun, flowing, not yet flawless: Lakers' league-best offense still has room to improve

Austin Reaves described it as "fun." Luka Doncic called the Lakers' effortless-looking offense as "flowing." And this is still the early stages of development for a team that brought in nine new players.

Through eight games, the Lakers have the most dynamic offense in the NBA. Led by Doncic, the Lakers are second in scoring with 122.5 points per game and first in offensive rating with 121.9 points per 100 possessions. The starting lineup of Doncic, Reaves, Walker Kessler, Ziaire Williams and Matisse Thybulle has a league-best 135.5 offensive rating among five-man groups that have played at least 40 minutes together entering Wednesday's game at Sacramento.

"Everything's as expected," guard Quentin Grimes said Monday after the Lakers hung 138 points in a 21-point win over the Miami Heat. "Winning, everybody's getting involved, everybody's making the right play, getting a lot of assists."

The Lakers (6-2) had 39 assists against the Heat, the most during JJ Redick's head-coaching tenure. Doncic is on a historic scoring binge; he is the first Laker since Kobe Bryant in 2007 to have five consecutive games of 35 or more points. While putting up a seemingly ho-hum 42 points against Miami, he also had a season-high 13 assists.

"It's a really good offense that we're playing right now," Redick said. "And a lot of that, of course, is Doncic and what he's able to do and bend the defense."

Doncic, the NBA's leading scorer at 38.3 points per game, does his damage early. He typically plays all 12 minutes of the opening quarter and leads the league with 15 points a game in the first quarter. Once he gets his shot going, teams send double teams to force the ball out of his hands. That's when Doncic can be particularly dangerous.

Read more: Luka Doncic's 42-point effort carries Lakers past Giannis Antetokounmpo and Heat

Doncic has always been lauded for his superior court vision. But the Lakers are still learning to see the same picture. The Lakers had 14 turnovers, including 11 from Doncic and Reaves, during a preseason game against the Denver Nuggets, who were aggressively trapping the Lakers' ballhandlers. The Lakers threw away a 25-point second-quarter lead on Oct. 30 when the Golden State Warriors ratcheted up the ball pressure.

Doncic's five turnovers a game are the second most in the league, and Reaves is third with 4.6 turnovers per game.

Some players are new to being on a team with guards who get blitzed nearly every play, Reaves said. It requires players to not only be comfortable making decisions to pass, drive or shoot, but they have to choose quickly. A moment's hesitation gives away the four-on-three advantage created by the double-team.

Redick praised Grimes' ability to keep advantages by driving decisively. Forward Sandro Mamukelashvili is also great at it, Redick said, as is guard Collin Sexton, who knows no speed other than full. The Lakers have also finished their advantages with Thybulle and Williams making27 of 58 (46.6%) three-point attempts combined.

"That's the beauty of our team," Williams said. "You could put different guys at different spots and everyone's able to make a play. All our guys are just dynamic and versatile. And everyone just wants to make the right play. No one wants to only shoot, there's no egos. And that's the fun part about it, you know? We all love to see each other succeed."

Williams missed three games because of a sore left foot but returned Monday with nine points, two rebounds and two assists off the bench. When Jake LaRavia jumped into the starting lineup, the Lakers were just as effective offensively as their first-choice lineup. When Doncic, Reaves, Kessler, Thybulle and LaRavia are together, the Lakers' 144.3 points per 100 possessions ranks first among lineups that have played at least 30 minutes.

Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo reaches through the hoop to block a reverse dunk by Lakers center Walker Kessler on Monday night. (Robert Gauthier / Los Angeles Times)

But numbers don't normalize until about 250 minutes, Redick believes.

"I think there's always room for improvement," he said Monday.

The Lakers have the most room for improvement on the defensive side. Their defensive rating of 114 points allowed per 100 possessions is tied with the Clippers for 20th in the NBA. They still rank 28th in rebounding, despite three consecutive double-doubles from Kessler, who responded after Redick challenged the center to be a larger rebounding presence.

"This team can become a great team," Redick said before Monday's win over the Heat. "That requires patience, that requires a lot of coaching and teaching and buy-in, and so that whole process takes time."
